newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips 1996 earnings hit by restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Philips 1996 earnings hit by restructuring.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Thursday reported a 1996 bottom line loss, ravaged by a net 1.3 billion guilders of extraordinary charges.

The company announced a net loss of 590 million guilders, against a 1995 net profit of 2.52 billion, and although it made a net profit of 723 million guilders from normal operations, this was well down on the 1995 profit of 2.68 billion guilders net from normal operations.
Philips chairman Cor Boonstra acknowledged the effect of the extraordinaries and added Philips had not responded quickly enough to market conditions.

"Part of this decline was caused by gearing up our organisation for growth which did not materialise. We were simply not quick enough in reacting to the market," said Boonstra in his first annual statement since becoming Philips' chairman in October.
"We do not blame the markets, nor our competitors, but rather take full responsibility for our lack of speed," he said.

Charges taken during the year included an 800 million pre-tax charge to restructure the Sound and Vision unit as well as another one billion guilders -- of which 600 million related to loss making German unit Grundig. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5014
